page_title: Web-based configuration and installation of BSD camera
page_content:
[TOC]


### Prerequisites
- The device and the computer are on the same LAN segment, and the computer can successfully ping the device's local IP address.
- Alternatively, if the device is equipped with a Wi-Fi module, switch it to AP mode; the computer should then connect to the AP hotspot and access the address `192.168.42.100`.
- The device is in the factory-shipped state (AI is licensed, and algorithms are loaded).

### Notes:
- Avoid configuration conflicts when enabling multiple AI functions linked to specific channels (e.g., ADAS, DSM, and BSDx4). For instance, assigning both ADAS and Right-side BSD to Channel 1 is not permitted, as this prevents the algorithms from functioning correctly. When enabling BSD for Right, Left, Front, and Rear positions simultaneously, check whether the "non-fisheye lens" mode is enabled for the Front and Rear BSDs. If the non-fisheye mode is *not* enabled for the Front and Rear BSDs, the Front BSD will conflict with the Right BSD, and the Rear BSD will conflict with the Left BSD; therefore, enabling all four non-fisheye BSD functions simultaneously in this scenario will result in operational errors. - Distinction between Left (L) BSD and Right (R) BSD:
Determine the orientation based on the direction the camera lens is facing; activate the BSD alarm for the side where the alert zone is located. For example, if the camera lens is facing the direction shown in the image below and the alert zone is on the left, the Left BSD (L BSD) must be activated.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=8baea9f65fbfe376cac0732ea1c456c9)

### Operation Steps:
###### 1. Camera Installation
##### The following example describes the installation and configuration of R BSD
1.1 R BSD Installation Angle and Positioning
Install the BSD camera on the front or rear section of either side of the vehicle. Ensure the camera base is aligned parallel/perpendicular to the vehicle body; ideally, mount it on a flat, vertical surface to avoid issues with the subsequent "vehicle body line" calibration. If such a surface is unavailable, detach the camera base and secure it using the provided screws or by welding. Then, reattach the camera to the base without fully tightening the screws on either side. For large trucks, the installation height should exceed 1.6 meters; for other vehicle types, adjust the height based on actual conditions. ![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=b6e174ef9547a2f95481fd8320c7cfff)
1.2 View the real-time channel feed. Ensure the vehicle body appears vertical in the image; if not, rotate the BSD camera or adjust it by pressing the sides to align it, and adjust the vertical angle by pressing the top or bottom of the camera until positioned correctly.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=a9f9dad480d0077ce759e61f219a9ebc)
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=3ef260668ab8f424f3aa9d785f6ba1f0)
1.3 Securing
Once the angle is adjusted, tighten the screws on the camera base to secure it in place.
Front and rear installation angles
1.4 Connect the camera's aviation connector to the video input port (or extension cable port) on the rear panel of the main unit—typically channel CH4. You may connect it to a different port based on the specific application scenario, provided you update the corresponding channel settings during configuration later; tighten the locking nut to secure the connection. 
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=2295214cb0e254cccdbf36307b7d42fd)![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=4ece45e35a7d1b69b2b77932c0fb51c3)

###### 2. Enabling the Function
2.1 Open a web browser on your computer, enter the device's local network IP address, input the login password "Adm_123", and click "Login".
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=8ea0998584866a5ec2cd3d6c7aec0858)
2.2 Click on the "General Settings" > "AI Settings" menu.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=b7d81120531706c7ef0205acb95ef209)![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=71b00505a4e3df47a953b5f4b2710f32)
2.3 In the "AI Settings" menu, enable the R-BSD function and link it to the corresponding BSD camera video input channel. Toggle the "Non-fisheye Lens" setting based on the type of BSD camera installed: enable this option for standard lenses and leave it disabled for fisheye (wide-angle distortion) lenses. Typically, standard lenses are used for Left and Right BSD, while fisheye lenses are used for Front and Rear BSD. Finally, click "Save" to activate the BSD function and reboot the main unit.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=2cd97eef85bd267b75d918f5e07e29fa)
Note: R BSD = Right BSD, L BSD = Left BSD, F BSD = Front BSD, B BSD = Rear BSD; enable the specific BSD function based on the actual installation scenario.


###### 3. Camera Configuration
Configuration of the BSD camera channel display (this step can be skipped if the image is already visible in the Web BSD calibration menu).
3.1 Return to the previous level and click "Basic Settings" >>> "Encoding Settings".
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=1f39c1aa24f33528190a17c2c95f6106)
3.2 Under "Channel Type," select the corresponding camera resolution (e.g., "1080P"). In this example, the L BSD camera is connected to channel CH4; confirm and save the settings, then reboot the device to verify that an image appears on channel CH4.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=19b8a42c18f1abbbc79332f612c66e74)

###### 4. Calibration Configuration
4.1 Click "General Settings" >>> "AI Settings" >>> "Right BSD Calibration" to open the BSD calibration page.
4.2 Click the four corners of the red zone box to adjust the size and shape of the box's sides; the yellow and green zone boxes (representing the three warning levels) are adjusted in the same way. Click the center of a zone box to move the entire box.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=25c69ed08f7e5066fc7be00f1d9faa53)
4.3 Click "Save" to complete calibration; restart the device for changes to take effect.
4.4 The procedure for Left, Front, and Rear BSD is similar: open the corresponding BSD calibration page in the AI section, then click and drag the area box to adjust it.


###### 5. Alarm Test
5.1 Alarm triggering in Test Mode (if this was already enabled during the ADAS parameter configuration, skip this step):
In the Web menu, navigate to "AI Settings" > "Test Mode," then save and restart the device.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=70330e028755d4e2072c2f7521d57f1b)
5.2 Alarm triggering in Normal Driving Mode: An alarm will occur when the configured thresholds are reached, provided the GPS antenna is connected and a GPS fix has been successfully established.

5.3 Log in to the V7 client to view alarm information.
![](http://pug2.4000329988.com/fqa/server/index.php?s=/api/attachment/visitFile&sign=c0551beadb29f849a0712859d62f32dd)
